podcast.body: "Beyond the Blue Horizon" by George Olsen, potentially released in 1930, is considered a contender for the first song to feature an artificial fade-out on a recording. This would predate the widespread use of electronic faders. "Maybe it was a 1930 song called Beyond the Blue Horizon from George Olson"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Firsts

podcast.body: This 1930 recording by George Olson's Big Band features an ending with the sound of a train receding into the distance, simulating a fade-out effect. This early example predates electronic fade-outs and relied on the band physically moving away from the recording horn. "This is a recording made in 1930 and it ends with a sound of a train receding into the distance."
